### Readiness view
The supplied filings support bounded financial, business, fundamental and historical liquidity work, together with validation of available evidence. They do not support completion of legal-capacity or full refinancing analysis without the governing agreements. Later-period information must remain separate, and preparation and extraction coverage are not fully certified.

### Analytical read-through
**Usable coverage.** K pages 118–124 locate the audit opinion, annual balance sheets, income statements, cash-flow statements, supplemental cash interest and taxes, and consolidation basis. K page 71 locates both the earnings and operating-cash-flow bridges to management's EBITDA As Defined, with explanatory footnotes continuing on page 72. K pages 162–165 locate segment definitions, external sales, earnings reconciliation, capital expenditures and geographic information. M pages 2, 5–6 and J pages 2, 6–7 establish distinct interim reporting bases. This supports a bounded financial foundation; it does not establish that every note, historical quarter or footnote has been extracted and validated.

**Business and transaction scope.** K page 4 calls the business a “designer, producer and supplier of highly engineered aircraft components”; page 5 describes the selective acquisition strategy. These are issuer descriptions, not independent market verification. K pages 131–132 locate Raptor Scientific's acquisition, financing with existing cash, segment assignment and preliminary purchase accounting. K pages 146–147, 150–153 locate financing activity and facility-level reporting. Acquisition disclosures outside the inspected spans remain downstream read requirements, not inferred facts.

**Debt and legal boundary.** K pages 144–145 distinguish “Gross Amount,” “Debt Issuance Costs,” “Original Issue (Discount) Premium” and “Net Amount.” K page 152 provides term-loan tranche maturities and pricing. K page 153 provides a fiscal-year maturity schedule excluding finance leases. These are useful inputs for mapping reported debt; they cannot be collapsed into one undifferentiated debt quantity. K pages 61–62 summarize restrictive and springing maintenance tests, but the operative definitions, exceptions, schedules, baskets and amendment interactions are absent. Availability disclosed by management is not independently established legal borrowing capacity.

**Liquidity timing.** The annual balance sheet includes cash and a dividend payable, while K page 63 explicitly dates the subsequent dividend settlement. K pages 62–63 and 152 separately identify the subsequent securitization draw. Evidence therefore supports a reporting-date bridge with subsequent events separately tagged, not silent netting or treating subsequent draws as as-of cash. K page 64 locates the contractual-obligations table, but its following explanatory footnotes were not inspected; modeled interest and obligation assumptions must be checked before quantitative use.

**Strongest contrary evidence to unrestricted readiness.** C page 1 states “legal_documents”: “none”. K page 112 repeatedly says “Incorporated by reference,” confirming that operative agreements referenced in the filing are not thereby included in this source set. K page 153 describes guarantor equivalence “As of the date of this Form 10-K,” not expressly the requested balance-sheet date. A legal-perimeter assertion cannot be promoted backward without schedules and effective dates. Missing preparation metadata and unreviewed source units also prevent any whole-pack fidelity certification.
